newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma arrests 47 political opponents over unrest.
newsitem.headline: Burma arrests 47 political opponents over unrest.

text.p: Burma's military government said on Tuesday it has arrested 47 members of the outlawed Communist Party and the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) party for their involvement in recent student unrest.

Lieutenant-General Khin Nyunt, Secretary One of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), told a rare news conference the government had arrested 34 members of the Burma Communist Party (BCP) and 13 NLD members in the wake of student unrest this month.

"We have uncovered who was behind the student unrest and other recent destructive activities in the country," Khin Nyunt told a news briefing during which the government presented a 60-page document detailing its findings of an investigation into the unrest.

"So far we have arrested 34 BCP underground agents and 13 NLD members for their involvement in creating the unrest," he said, adding that three BCP agents were still at large, two of whom were university students.
Khin Nyunt said nine civilians who were arrested following recent demonstrations had been released.
The BCP, formerly a key political force led by Thakin Than Tun -- an uncle of NLD leader Aung San Suu Kyi -- was outlawed after Burma became independent in 1948.
The NLD, co-founded in 1988 by Suu Kyi, won a landslide election in 1990 but has never been allowed to take power after the SLORC refused to recognise the results of the poll.
Nearly 2,000 university students took to the street in early December at the start of a series of the biggest anti-government demonstrations seen in Rangoon since 1988.
Last week two bombs exploded at a Buddhist site in a Rangoon suburb, killing five people and wounding 17.
The government has accused the exiled students, outlawed Burmese communists and the NLD of instigating the protests.
It also accused exiled student and ethnic groups for plotting the bombings in an effort to destabilise the country. The Thailand-based groups have denied involvement.
